races.title: State House, District 109
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Donnie Loftis
cands.bio: Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 109 (part of Gaston County) since November 2021. Former Gaston County commissioner and chair of the CaroMont Health board. U.S. Army veteran who served during the Iraq war. Lost his 2026 re-election bid.

controversies.text: Loftis went to Washington for the Jan. 6, 2021 rally. He wrote on Facebook that he "got gassed three times and was at the entrance when they breached the door." In October 2021 he said he peacefully exercised his rights, had "zero involvement in the rioting" and condemned the storming. WRAL reported no charge against him.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Loftis was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no statements from him on data centers, property taxes, land buying, growth, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or police, because he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys and his campaign site is general. We found no specific actions by him on these issues. The list of bills he sponsored did not load. We did not find his early-life details, his business career outside public office, or any endorsements for 2026. He signed the U.S. Term Limits Pledge in 2024, which does not bear directly on these issues.

qual.background: Served in the NC House from November 2021 to January 2027, including on the Appropriations committees. Earlier served as a Gaston County commissioner (Wikipedia says chair of the board) and chaired the CaroMont Health board. U.S. Army veteran of the Iraq war.
qual.why: He has about five years of legislative service, including Appropriations assignments, plus local elected office. The sources show no law, policy or budget career, and board and committee chairs add nothing to the score.

cands.name: Mark D. Carver
cands.bio: Democrat who won the North Carolina House District 109 seat in 2026, defeating incumbent Donnie Loftis. Worked 25 years at Kelly-Springfield Tire, serving as a shop steward and elected United Steel Workers division chairman. Has taught college history for 22 years, 20 of them at Gaston College.
cands.gaps: We found no stated or documented position from Carver on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state, investor or foreign land buyers, immigration enforcement or H-1B, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site has issue pages on education, affordability and housing, but only the summary blurbs were available, not the detail pages. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. He has held no prior public office, so there is no legislative record to review. His biography does not give his birth year or when he began living in Gaston County. His birthplace and upbringing come only from his own campaign biography.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign biography says he was born and raised in Fayetteville, NC, and he has worked and taught in North Carolina for decades, including 20 years at Gaston College.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Worked 25 years at Kelly-Springfield Tire, rising to vacation-replacement supervisor, shop steward and elected USW Division Chairman, and served on the 1996 contract negotiating committee. Earned a history degree and a graduate degree, then taught college history for 22 years. No prior legislative or local elected office is shown.
qual.why: He has no prior government office, so he falls in the middle-to-low range. Elected union leadership, contract bargaining and long teaching experience count for something, but they are not legislative or budget work.
qual.label: He has no prior government office, so he falls in the middle-to-low range. Elected union leadership, contract bargaining and long teaching experience count for something, but they are not legislative or budget work.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says communities depend on firefighters, EMTs and police officers and that "we must stand by those who risk life and limb in service of our great state." It gives no specific pay, pension or penalty proposals in the text available.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says North Carolina's rivers, mountains and wildlife "must be guarded against pollution, abuse, and deforestation." It lists no specific growth or rezoning proposals in the text available.
